Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a concise, denominator-first evidence card in the “Connector-access-check archive” for future Helio Start operating reviews. Summarize what the first fully mature post-check cohort established about credential-related failures, and clearly separate that operational finding from any longer-horizon business outcomes the cohort did not establish.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Connector-access-check archive — First fully mature post-check cohort", "folder": "Connector-access-check archive", "body": "Evidence card — Helio Start
As of 2028-01-01

Denominator first
- Completed applications: 92.
- Admitted workspaces: 68.
- Supported first integrations within seven days: 59 of 68 admitted.
- Credential-related nonactivators: 3 of the 68 admitted workspaces (3 of the 9 admitted workspaces that did not integrate within seven days).
- Comparator: 18 credential-related stalls among 147 prior admitted workspaces.

Operational finding
The first fully mature post-check cohort observed fewer credential-related stalls than the prior admitted population, while the admitted-workspace denominator remained intact. This supports treating connector-access/credential readiness as a material operational friction point and retaining the check. The 11 Customer Success contacts across 8 admitted workspaces are a separate support-contact measure, not a count of credential failures.

Evidence boundary
This is a standalone connector-check observation; it is not pooled with the validated six-cohort activation series, and cohort overlap has not been established. The cohort does not establish mature retention, first-paid conversion, day-90 outcomes, forecastable revenue, paid-acquisition performance, or readiness for a pipeline target. Those longer-horizon business outcomes require separate cohorts and complete observation windows."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_170_02", "path": "args", "criterion": "The body gives a denominator-first comparison for credential-related failures among admitted workspaces: 3 of 68 in the first fully mature cohort after the connector-access check (about 4.4%) versus 18 of 147 in the prior cohort (about 12.2%). It accurately interprets the lower post-check rate as operational evidence supporting the connector-access check, without presenting the comparison as proof of broader causality.

The body clearly and explicitly states that the mature-cohort result did not establish mature retention, paid conversion, or revenue performance. Missing any of these three limitations, or claiming that any was established, must fail.", "value": {"title": "Connector-access-check archive — First fully mature post-check cohort", "folder": "Connector-access-check archive", "body": "Evidence card — Helio Start
As of 2028-01-01

Denominator first
- Completed applications: 92.
- Admitted workspaces: 68.
- Supported first integrations within seven days: 59 of 68 admitted.
- Credential-related nonactivators: 3 of the 68 admitted workspaces (3 of the 9 admitted workspaces that did not integrate within seven days).
- Comparator: 18 credential-related stalls among 147 prior admitted workspaces.

Operational finding
The first fully mature post-check cohort observed fewer credential-related stalls than the prior admitted population, while the admitted-workspace denominator remained intact. This supports treating connector-access/credential readiness as a material operational friction point and retaining the check. The 11 Customer Success contacts across 8 admitted workspaces are a separate support-contact measure, not a count of credential failures.

Evidence boundary
This is a standalone connector-check observation; it is not pooled with the validated six-cohort activation series, and cohort overlap has not been established. The cohort does not establish mature retention, first-paid conversion, day-90 outcomes, forecastable revenue, paid-acquisition performance, or readiness for a pipeline target. Those longer-horizon business outcomes require separate cohorts and complete observation windows."}}]}

It cautiously says the cohort “observed fewer credential-related stalls” and that this “supports” retaining the check, without claiming broader causality. It also explicitly states: “The cohort does not establish mature retention, first-paid conversion... [or] forecastable revenue.”"}]}
